body.estimand_functional: Under normal-link distributional parallel trends and no anticipation, the causal estimand is identified by the observed-law functional \(\overline\Delta=15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\{H(r_{\ell1},r_{\ell2},r_{\ell3})-r_{\ell4}\}\). On the common-rarity class this equals \(15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\{\Phi[\Phi^{-1}(\rho c_{\ell1})+\Phi^{-1}(\rho c_{\ell2})-\Phi^{-1}(\rho c_{\ell3})]-\rho c_{\ell4}\}\). Its zero-safe observed-count plug-in is \(15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\widehat\Delta^E_{\ell}=15^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{15}\{H(\widetilde r_{\ell1},\widetilde r_{\ell2},\widetilde r_{\ell3})-\widetilde r_{\ell4}\}\), where \(\widetilde r_{\ell j}=(K_{\ell j}+1/2)/(n_{\ell j}+1)\).

sampling_model.design: The fifteen pre/post pairs and four roles are fixed before outcomes; independent complete blocks are split by an outcome-independent rule into sixty disjoint role samples.
sampling_model.units: For pair \(\ell\) and role \(j\), \(n_{\ell j}\) block-level threshold indicators are observed, with \(n_{\ell j}/n\to\pi_{\ell j}>0\).
sampling_model.treatment: Roles are treated-pre, control-post, control-pre, and treated-post; normal-link distributional parallel trends and no anticipation identify the untreated treated-post distribution.
sampling_model.overlap: All role counts are independent by construction; inference for overlapping original blocks is outside this version.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cell probabilities use the add-half estimator \(\widetilde r_{\ell j}=(K_{\ell j}+1/2)/(n_{\ell j}+1)\); no known nuisance probability is assumed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies the transformed-CDF counterfactual, while Assumption 5 requires a uniform positive transformed-density lower bound and Theorem 2 gives \(\sqrt N\) Gaussian weak convergence under interior regularity.
The main theorem bounds the inverse Mills ratio on a half-plane, and its corollary bounds derivatives.
The paper proves monotonicity, complete monotonicity, and Turán-type inequalities for the Gaussian Mills ratio.
The paper derives second-order limits and characterizes standard-bootstrap failure for functionals with a zero first derivative.
Rare truncation experiments admit Gaussian or Poisson limits under different retained-count regimes.
Exact inversion gives finite-sample-valid intervals for continuous real functions of multinomial probability vectors, with a Monte Carlo computational approximation.

Distribution-regression DiD makes the link specification part of the counterfactual distribution construction but does not give the exact equality set between the standard-normal and multiplicative counterfactual maps.
Nonlinear DiD models and estimators depend on a selected functional form, without an exact pointwise probit-versus-multiplicative coincidence characterization.

Parallel-trends conclusions can be sensitive to functional form; the paper studies invariance restrictions rather than the exact normal-link-versus-multiplicative equality set for this distributional-DiD map.
Confidence regions can be optimized for expected size, whereas the present rational outer interval proves only simultaneous validity and an expected-diameter order.

Chen--Stein theory supplies quantitative Poisson approximation bounds, whereas the present fixed-dimensional product-Poisson transition is derived directly and propagated through the smoothed nonlinear statistic.

body.tldr: Under the published normal-link identification assumptions, the causal crime-free DTT equals an observed-law map, while the add-half statistic is a separate zero-safe plug-in. Globally on the open probability cube, the normal-link and multiplicative maps agree exactly on the two planes \(p_1=p_3\) or \(p_2=p_3\), with a cancellation-safe signed-rectangle factorization. On every fixed positive compact coefficient interval, a proved Gaussian-tail transfer controls the value, gradient, and Hessian uniformly; on the comparable-rarity box the common-cutoff coefficient is \(C_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})\), including both planes. The Gaussian drift frontiers, bounded-count product-Poisson limits, and rational outer intervals apply to the deliberately independent sixty-role split design.

project_justification.gap: Djuazon and Tsyawo's Assumptions 1--2 identify the fixed-threshold standard-normal DTT functional, but their interior theory does not cover probabilities shrinking to zero. Existing nonlinear-DiD and functional-form analyses do not characterize the exact pointwise equality set between the standard-normal and multiplicative counterfactual maps, and one-dimensional inverse-Mills bounds alone do not provide the compact-uniform mixed value, gradient, and Hessian transfer needed for rare-panel inference.
project_justification.niche: The project separates a global population geometry, valid for every \(p_1,p_2,p_3\in(0,1)\), from a comparable-rarity refinement and a fixed-compact Gaussian-tail transfer that connect cancellation distance to Gaussian and bounded-count sampling frontiers.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the global signed-rectangle factorization and exact two-plane zero set, the fixed-compact tail-transfer lemma, and the uniform common-cutoff expansion on the declared coefficient box. It then propagates those analytic results through pairwise and aggregate Gaussian limits, a product-Poisson transition, and certified finite-sample outer inference under the predeclared split-role experiment.

body.related_work: Djuazon and Tsyawo (2026) supply, through Assumptions 1--2 and Theorem 1, the causal identification baseline specialized here to a standard-normal link and threshold zero; that population identity is not a novelty claim. Their Assumption 5 requires a positive lower bound on the transformed density, whereas \(\phi(q(\rho_nc_{\ell j,n}))\to0\) uniformly on the comparable-rarity box, so their interior Theorem 2 does not cover the present rare array. The fixed-probability split-role Gaussian proposition is proved independently and is an analogue, not a claim of membership in their original sampling class. Pinelis (2019) and Baricz (2008) develop one-dimensional inverse-Mills bounds and monotonicity tools; the global signed-rectangle identity, its exact two-plane zero set, and the fixed-compact normal-tail transfer are proved here. Fernández-Val, Meier, van Vuuren, and Vella (2024) and Wooldridge (2023) develop link-dependent nonlinear DiD constructions, while Roth and Sant'Anna (2023) study sensitivity of parallel trends to functional form; none supplies the exact pointwise standard-normal-versus-multiplicative equality frontier proved by the global factorization theorem. Chen and Fang (2019) analyze higher-order behavior under degeneracy in Gaussian experiments, while Marohn (2001) and Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989) provide broader Poisson-limit and Poisson-approximation context; the smoothed product-Poisson statistic here is derived directly for sixty independent rare cells. Sachs, Gabriel, and Fay (2026) motivate exact inversion for nonlinear functions of discrete probabilities, and Schafer and Stark (2009) study expected-size optimality; the present rational outer algorithm proves finite termination, simultaneous coverage, and an expected-diameter order, but no optimality claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The literal statement that every all-full table with all \(n_j\leq6\) must yield an empty retained list is false without a calibration restriction: with \(n_j=1\) and \(\beta=1/2\), the admissible point \(p_j=1/4\) has deviance \(8\log4<16=8/\beta\). The interval theorem therefore uses its explicit sufficient inequality for all-full empty-list behavior; all-zero retention is unaffected. The global Lipschitz constant is deliberately enormous, so finite termination is a certificate rather than a practical runtime guarantee. The compact-tail lemma supplies existence of a common cutoff and constants on each fixed interval, not numerically optimized finite-rarity constants.
body.honest_scope: The pointwise cancellation theorem is a population result for every \(p_1,p_2,p_3\in(0,1)\); it needs neither rarity nor sampling. The fixed-compact tail-transfer lemma is uniform on any deterministic \([d,D]\subset(0,\infty)\), while the sharper complete-error expansion \(C_{\rho,\ell}=-u^{-2}+O(u^{-4})\) uses the declared comparable-rarity box and rare limit. Causal interpretation additionally requires normal-link distributional parallel trends and no anticipation. The Gaussian and product-Poisson laws require coefficient and positive role-share limits, Bernoulli role sampling, and mutual independence of the predeclared pair--role samples; the rational interval uses its separately stated finite-sample premises. None of these sampling results supplies covariance formulas or joint rare-event limits for overlapping original blocks. The conservative aggregate interval must include zero in the published 37-treated-block application, so no finite-sample power or field-tier recovery claim is made.
